checks: Through-point reduction tightens each proper closed containing halfspace by parallel translation. For a fixed normal the pointwise limsup of the closed-cap indicators is bounded by the limiting indicator, also on positive-mass fiber traces; finite measure and reverse Fatou give upper semicontinuity. An infimum of upper semicontinuous functions is upper semicontinuous.

If a closed halfspace contains a convex combination, its affine margin cannot be strictly negative at every positively weighted input. This proves convexity of the depth superlevel. Compact S and upper semicontinuity give attainment; any own-fiber interior ball contributes at least half its volume for every containing halfspace, or its full volume for a constant trace. Strict separation outside conv(S) and positivity of Q make the ambient superlevel D compact. Only D∩S is used as the actual set of maximizers.

At an own-fiber boundary point, select a nonzero supporting normal in the continuous coordinates. The anchored support slope bounds every fiber support, so the opposite closed halfspace through the point has only empty or supporting traces. A proper supporting hyperplane is Lebesgue null in every d-dimensional fiber, also for interval endpoints when d=1.

The positive finite energy root is continuous on each open own-fiber interior by finite concavity. The nonempty compact D∩S avoids the boundaries and splits into finitely many compact fiber slices. This gives an attaining positive R. For two distinct maximizing marks in one slice, strict fixed-body concavity raises the energy root at their feasible midpoint.

For a positive anchored relation, completeness gives q∈P, the input interior balls give an interior ball in the Minkowski sum at the averaged mark, and anchored inclusion puts the sum in K_q. Convexity of D makes the target an actual deepest point. Both endpoints of the energy comparison equal R, so equality forces K_q to be the whole Minkowski sum and all centered input bodies to be positive homothets. For a centered homothety of factor c>0 energy scales by c^d; equality to the same R^d>0 forces c=1. The centered Minkowski sum is then the common centered body, and uniqueness at q identifies its mark. Dropping zero coefficients proves J=conv(J)∩Z^n. No global affine law for the marks, or shape relation between unrelated bases, is inferred.

Every distinct same-parity pair has an integer midpoint, and the proven relation holds for it. The three bodies involved are translates of a single body, so the ordinary centroid of the midpoint is the mean of the endpoint centroids. This uses only translation covariance of centroids, not a general Minkowski additivity claim. Thus the labeled finite centroid graph is midpoint closed on every required pair.

The weighted atomic center is a fixed graph point in S. Every ambient containing halfspace restricts to an intrinsic containing halfspace or the whole graph, so its captured centroid weight is at least M_J/k(J). In each counted fiber, a nonconstant trace contains the cap parallel to it through the centroid and pays at least (d/(d+1))^d of the fiber volume; a constant trace containing the centroid pays the full volume. Distinct base fibers are disjoint, and remaining fibers add nonnegative mass. Taking the infimum preserves this weak bound, and maximizing on S transfers it to Q. The paying point need not be a marked deepest point, and no strict or whole-family-mass bound is needed.

When n=0 the sole base has slope zero and one occupied parity, the anchored relation is tautological at its unique mark, and the atomic graph is a singleton. As a separate exact d=1 check, for K−y=[−l,r], l,r>0, the integral is (l+r)/((1−al)(1+ar)). Its denominator is maximized at a=(r−l)/(2lr), giving energy 4lr/(l+r), strictly concave in y; a centroid cap has at least half the length. For n=0,d=1 the unique deepest mark is the interval midpoint and the claimed payment is exact.

dependencies.hypotheses: At p fix the unit continuous-coordinate normal. The source family is finite, each body compact convex and nonempty, and the global anchored inclusion specializes to every representation of p. This fact allows arbitrary base affine rank, including n=0, so the supporting slope applies.

Each own body and the Minkowski sum is full-dimensional and compact; all marks used are interior. The exact positive-denominator infimum agrees with the attained energy in this fact. Its affine covariance at Q=cI gives the power c^d and its inclusion test has the required common interior mark.

All retained weights are positive and sum to one, with d≥1 and interior marks. The containing-body specialization applies to the actual full-dimensional K_q containing the Minkowski sum. Its fixed-body strict concavity applies to two distinct interior marks of one K_p. No global joint-fiber domain beyond the anchored inclusion is needed.

Finite nonempty graph with strictly positive fiber volume weights and exactly k(J) occupied labels. Every distinct equally labeled pair has its actual geometric midpoint in the graph by the proved centroid identity. The general finite-label result works in any affine hull, including rank zero and whole-space traces. Only its weak depth conclusion is used.

Only the ordinary Grünbaum inequality (4) is used, for uniform volume on each full-dimensional K_p with its ordinary centroid. This requires d≥1 and imposes no base dimension, affine rank, or symmetry restriction. If (4) is read solely in the positive-base setting of that fact, apply it to the unique integer fiber of the full-dimensional product [−1/2,1/2]×K_p in one auxiliary base dimension. In d=1 the inequality is the interval midpoint bound.
